instruction: In the MUST_VISIT.xlsx spreadsheet on the desktop, add two new column headers: type "Rating" in cell E1 and "Cuisine" in cell F1.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to search Hong Kong restaurants on Google Maps but encountered SSL certificate errors (NET:ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID) in Chrome. Spent all 50 turns trying workarounds including Firefox, terminal curl, and file manager, but never accessed the internet successfully. Never entered any data into the spreadsheet.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome and type URLs, switch between windows, open terminal and type commands, interact with file manager, read text files in gedit
metadata.failure_analysis: SSL certificate errors blocked all web access in the VM. Model spent all turns trying to bypass the connection error instead of falling back to local tasks. Never interacted with the spreadsheet.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a minimal spreadsheet editing task: just adding two column headers. Tests whether model can navigate to specific cells and type text in LibreOffice Calc without requiring internet.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to cells E1 and F1 in the spreadsheet and typing header text. Evaluator checks each cell with fuzzy string matching, giving 0.5 partial credit per correct header.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cells E1 and F1 from MUST_VISIT.xlsx using openpyxl, matching the exact cells specified in the instruction.
Postconfig properly activates LibreOffice Calc window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Metric correctly accesses the expected parameter directly (expected.get('expected_e1')), which is proper for type='rule' where get_rule returns the rules dict.
Expected values ('Rating' for E1, 'Cuisine' for F1) exactly match the instruction requirements.
Both instruction requirements are fully covered with appropriate partial credit (0.5 per correct header).
Case-insensitive substring matching provides reasonable fuzzy comparison for header text verification.
